elements.element: Renewal requires mutual written agreement unless every conditional automatic-renewal element below is met.
elements.evidence: Renewal remains automatic ("This Agreement will automatically renew for additional 1-year terms unless Customer gives written notice of non-renewal at least sixty (60) days prior..."), and the conditional automatic-renewal elements are not all satisfied: the opt-out window is 60 days (not ≤30) and there is no Vendor renewal reminder. To reach preferred, either convert to renewal by mutual written agreement or satisfy every automatic-renewal condition.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, each renewal term is no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Renewal is for "additional 1-year terms", i.e. 12 months, unchanged by the edit.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer may opt out on no more than 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The inserted mechanic requires notice "at least sixty (60) days prior to the end of the then-current term" — 60 days exceeds the 30-day preferred ceiling. Repair by changing "sixty (60)" to "thirty (30)" in the non-renewal sentence.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Vendor must remind Customer at least 60 days before renewal.
elements.evidence: No reminder obligation appears anywhere in the rendered paragraph 4(a); Kubient is not required to notify Customer in advance of any automatic renewal.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: paragraph 4(a) renews on existing terms and contains no renewal price-uplift mechanic (compensation is a revenue share set in an Exhibit), so no cap is triggered.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: Inserted operative text: "unless Customer gives written notice of non-renewal at least sixty (60) days prior to the end of the then-current term" — a Customer non-renewal right with a 60-day window, exactly at the fallback ceiling and applicable to the end of the Initial Term as well as each renewal term. The deterministic check reporting "number not found" is a false negative; the numeral "sixty (60)" is present in the rendered clause.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: renewal is on the same terms with no price-increase mechanic in the renewal provision, so no 5% cap is required and none was volunteered.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete: the insertion supplies the previously absent non-renewal mechanic at exactly 60 days, and the price-uplift element is conditional and untriggered because renewal occurs on existing terms with no uplift language.

Preferred level fails on three counts: renewal is still automatic rather than by mutual written agreement, the opt-out window is 60 rather than ≤30 days, and there is no Vendor obligation to remind Customer at least 60 days before renewal.

Minimal: the edit inserts a single conditional clause into the existing renewal sentence, adds no survival tail, expense, procedure or pricing language, and deletes nothing — the 90-day for-any-reason right, the Initial Term lock-in, the material-breach and insolvency rights, and Kubient's fee entitlement all survive verbatim.

Preserves intent: the new Customer-only non-renewal right operates alongside, and does not contradict, the mutual termination rights in 4(a)-(b); no defined term, cross-reference or commercial mechanic is left dangling.

Note for the drafter (rationale-level, not a defect at the chosen level): moving to "thirty (30) days" and adding a Vendor reminder obligation at least 60 days before each renewal would lift this to the preferred position.
